scope: Theorem 6.1 (Isotropic improvement) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 86. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider the tangent data of Proposition 4.7, with 0 < k ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ d < 1, either in version 1, where j = 1, or in version 2 with j = 2 and optimized narrowness ℓ = 0. In every substantial residual of the reference path one can, after passing to a subsequence, find a packet Q = Qs, of thickness a = N−s and time length h ∼log,N ak, and a time-improvement candidate of thickness a2 = ahe2 , e2 > 0. The candidate has incidence mass at least hνQ K  a2 a d , K = No(1) . Writing the candidate as Pnew, its bounds |Pnew| ≤ Ka2 and |∂wPnew| ≤ K hold on its assigned trajectories throughout the same h-length block. The hidden derivative is bounded below by K−1 on the counted incidences, and its hidden curvature is at most K/a2. In version 1 the test has the special form w − F(t, y), with F quadratic. In version 2 it is a quadratic in (t, y, w).
